channel.title: Kompas — News for people abroad
channel.description: Asylum and deportations, extraditions and wanted lists, in-absentia cases and registers, the border and new laws used to prosecute people who have left. Everything that affects the safety of people who have left.

item.title: Ukrainian Lyubov Rozhanskaya released from detention in Astana and has already left Kazakhstan
item.description: She was detained at the airport on 1 October at Russia's request. Her lawyer says the detention period expired and no preventive measure was chosen. She was freed on 4 October and is heading to Odesa. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Khabarovsk journalist Alexander Simontsev detained in the US; he and his family had applied for asylum
item.description: ICE officers detained him on a road in Arkansas, his wife said; where he was taken is unknown. According to her, hearings on the asylum case are scheduled for 2028. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: UN Committee against Torture demands Kazakhstan not hand Yulia Emelyanova over to Russia
item.description: On 8 October the committee applied urgent measures on the complaint of the former Navalny campaign activist, her lawyer said. She remains in custody in Almaty and the extradition decision remains in force. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Czech citizen Vitaly Demidchik, who came from Prague to visit his sick mother, detained in Belarus
item.description: According to Nasha Niva, he was detained after crossing the border on 30 June and is charged under Article 361-3 of the Criminal Code over transfers in support of Ukraine. He is held in SIZO No. 1 in Minsk. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Former police investigator in Nizhny Novgorod region charged with forging documents for asylum seekers
item.description: The case under Part 1 of Article 327 of the Criminal Code has reached the Moskovsky District Court of Nizhny Novgorod, Mediazona reports. The FSB claims he produced documents on political persecution for refugee status abroad. — Mediazona

item.title: Belarus prosecutor general: about 2 500 people convicted under "extremism" articles in a year and a half
item.description: According to Prosecutor General Dmitry Gora, about 2 000 criminal cases were opened in a year and a half. Since 2022, in absentia cases against more than 150 people have been sent to court. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Delfi: Latvia's foreign ministry decides to declare Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata
item.description: According to Delfi, the journalist has lived in Latvia since 2014. Foreign Minister Baiba Braže said the decision was based on information from the competent authorities. — Meduza

item.title: Boris Grebenshchikov fined 15 thousand roubles over an interview with Meduza
item.description: According to Mediazona, Moscow's Khoroshevsky District Court fined the musician for cooperating with an “undesirable” organisation. Grebenshchikov left Russia in 2020 and lives in the UK. — Mediazona

item.title: Kaliningrad man who swam to Lithuania to seek asylum and was sent back gets 6 years in a penal colony
item.description: According to Mediazona, the Baltic Fleet Military Court sentenced a 68-year-old man from Neman to six years over anti-war posts. Lithuania's border service returned him to Russia the same day. — Mediazona

item.title: Interior Ministry puts Samara journalist Sergei Leibgrad, named a “foreign agent” a month ago, on its wanted list
item.description: According to Mediazona, this means a criminal case has been opened against him in absentia; what it concerns is unknown. The journalist emigrated to Israel in 2022. — Mediazona

item.title: Yevgeny Nakaznenko, who spent a year in a Kazakh deportation prison at Russia's request, has left for France
item.description: According to Mediazona, he left on a humanitarian visa, as he told the outlet Vot Tak. Russia had put him on its wanted list over justifying terrorism and military “fakes”. — Mediazona

item.title: Journalist Andrei Loshak remanded in absentia in a case of justifying terrorism
item.description: According to OVD-Info, the decision was made by Moscow's Basmanny District Court (Article 205.2, Part 2). What prompted the case is not yet known. — OVD-Info

item.title: Masyanya creator Oleg Kuvaev sentenced in absentia to four years in a penal colony
item.description: According to Mediazona, the Nevsky District Court in St Petersburg convicted him under Articles 330.1 and 280.4. The case concerns an episode in which the heroine urges Russian soldiers to surrender. — Mediazona

item.title: Perm activist Leonid Melekhin, deported from the US, sentenced to six years in a penal colony
item.description: According to Mediazona, the Central District Military Court in Yekaterinburg convicted him of justifying terrorism (Article 205.2). The trial was held behind closed doors. — Mediazona

item.title: Entrepreneur charged with treason over the military levy he paid in Ukraine
item.description: According to Mediazona, cited by OVD-Info, this is the first known case in which paying taxes to the Ukrainian budget became grounds for a treason charge (Article 275). — OVD-Info

item.title: Germany refuses a Russian student a study visa, citing a 'security threat'
item.description: According to the Molniya project, the embassy in Moscow turned down a graduate of the HSE design programme. The rights group calls it a dangerous precedent for art students. — Meduza

item.title: Ukrainian Lyubov Rozhanskaya detained in Astana at Russia's request; Russia seeks her extradition
item.description: According to DW, cited by Mediazona, Russia accuses her of attempting to abduct her grandson. Her lawyers say she did not know about the case and has never been to Russia. — Mediazona

item.title: Prosecutors seek 5 years 11 months in absentia for Masyanya creator Oleg Kuvaev
item.description: According to Mediazona, he is charged under Articles 330.1 and 280.4 over an episode in which Masyanya urges Russian soldiers to surrender. His lawyer says Kuvaev was not notified of the case. — Mediazona

item.title: Georgian court releases on bail Sergei Furgal's former aide, whom Russia wants extradited
item.description: According to The Insider, Mikhail Timofeev was released on bail of 50 thousand lari and barred from leaving Georgia. In September a court approved his extradition, but the UN Human Rights Committee told Georgia not to extradite him. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Justice Ministry adds Zhanna Nemtsova and Navalny Team to 'foreign agents' register
item.description: According to OVD-Info, Circassian activist Rustam Khuazhev and the resource Reanimatsiya were also added. In September Nemtsova was placed on an international wanted list. — OVD-Info

item.title: Tomsk court remands producer Elena Matushevskaya in custody over donations to FBK
item.description: According to OVD-Info, investigators say she transferred money to FBK seven times, 3500 roubles in total (Article 282.3). Matushevskaya lived in Serbia; her defence will appeal. — OVD-Info

item.title: Founder of Buryat independence movement sentenced in absentia to 20 years
item.description: A military court in Chita sentenced US-based Marina Khankhalaeva under Articles 282.2 and 205.5, Buryatia's police said, 7x7 reports. According to the outlet, the verdict was handed down on 27 August. — 7x7

item.title: Belarus designates YouTube channel with Sergei Tikhanovsky's poems 'extremist'
item.description: The Oshmyany district court made the decision on 25 September, according to the updated Information Ministry list, Mediazona Belarus reports. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Astra founder Anastasia Chumakova sentenced in absentia to seven years in a penal colony
item.description: Mediazona reports that the Zavolzhsky District Court in Ulyanovsk convicted her of spreading military 'fakes' and breaching the 'foreign agent' law. The journalist has lived outside Russia for several years. — Mediazona

item.title: Former TV2 employee who lived in Serbia detained in Krasnoyarsk over donations to FBK
item.description: Elena Matushevskaya is suspected of taking part in an 'extremist' organisation, Novaya Gazeta Europe reports, citing Govorit NeMoskva. She had come to Krasnoyarsk for work; a custody hearing is expected in Tomsk. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Leaked Turkmen interior ministry wanted list shows persecution of critics abroad
item.description: According to Turkmen.news and OCCRP, 613 people were on the wanted list at the end of 2022, 93 of them facing political charges, including 'terrorism'. — Turkmen.news

item.title: Yaroslavl court sentences exiled LGBT activist to 4 years in absentia
item.description: The Kirovsky district court found Yaroslav Sirotkin guilty of taking part in an 'extremist' organisation (Part 2 of Article 282.2) and of breaching the 'foreign agent' law, 7x7 reports, citing Pervy Otdel. — 7x7

item.title: Russia agrees with five CIS countries to share data on people the authorities deem 'extremists'
item.description: The prosecutors general of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan signed an agreement to share information on organisations and individuals, Meduza reports, citing RBC. — Meduza

item.title: Moscow court arrests journalist Yury Dud in absentia on a charge of justifying terrorism
item.description: The Basmanny court arrested Dud in absentia under Part 2 of Article 205.2, the Moscow courts' press service said. The Investigative Committee claims the case stems from his interview with RDK founder Denis Kapustin. — Mediazona

item.title: More than 150 human rights defenders urge Kazakhstan not to extradite Emelyanova and Movlaev to Russia
item.description: According to Vlast, the appeal was signed by 155 people, among them members of OVD-Info and First Department. They ask for a diplomatic corridor to a safe third country. — Vlast.kz

item.title: Protest in New York against Kazakhstan extraditing activists Emelyanova and Movlaev to Russia
item.description: According to Azattyq Asia, Iuliia Emelianova and Mansur Movlaev have been held in a remand prison in Almaty for over a year after being detained at Moscow's request. Kazakhstan earlier refused Movlaev asylum. — Azattyq Asia

item.title: FSB opens a case for membership of a terrorist organisation against London-based Ksenia Maksimova
item.description: Maksimova heads the Russian Democratic Society in the UK. The FSB claims she raised money through the movement "in the interests of the Kyiv regime". She was put on the wanted list on 16 September. — Mediazona

item.title: In Belarus, five volunteers of the Kalinouski Regiment sentenced in absentia to 12 to 20 years
item.description: According to Viasna, the Minsk City Court handed down the sentence on 14 September. The charges include conspiracy to seize power and membership of a terrorist organisation. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: 10 Belarusian political prisoners, freed and expelled to Lithuania, apply for protection in Poland
item.description: According to Reform.news, 25 political prisoners were freed on 16 September and all were forcibly taken to Lithuania. Nine applied for international protection in Warsaw and one in Bialystok. — Reform.news

item.title: Finland may deport to Russia a family who left over their anti-war stance
item.description: According to Current Time, a mother and son left in 2022 and collected aid for Ukrainians in emigration; in Russia they face criminal prosecution. They were refused asylum and are suing the migration agency. — Radio Liberty

item.title: IT specialist living in Israel detained at Belarus–Lithuania border over YouTube subscriptions
item.description: According to Reform.news, citing the man himself, a phone check found subscriptions to two YouTube channels designated “extremist materials”. He spent three days in a temporary detention centre before a court fined him. — Reform.news

item.title: Georgia expels to Armenia Belarusian Lev Mikheev, who had sought asylum since 2021
item.description: Mikheev says that on 25 September he was driven to the Armenian border, where he was held on a wanted notice at Minsk's request. Rights defender Roman Kisliak calls it in effect an enforced disappearance. — Reform.news

item.title: “Khodorkovsky LIVE” designated a “foreign agent”
item.description: The Justice Ministry added the news YouTube channel, which has more than 3 million subscribers, to its register of “foreign agents”. — Mediazona

item.title: YouTuber “Ded Arkhimed” arrested in absentia over “fakes” and foreign-agent rules
item.description: A court in Ivanovo ordered the arrest in absentia of the 53-year-old blogger on charges of spreading army “fakes” and evading “foreign agent” obligations. — Mediazona

item.title: Border officers extract phone data via Bluetooth
item.description: Equipment used at Russian border checks can pull call history and contact lists from travellers’ phones over Bluetooth. — Mediazona
